content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any project documents related to radiator aging, radiation tolerance, transparency, maintenance, and detector lifetime. Extract the three allowed radiator candidates and their relevant material constraints."},{"id":"s2","description":"From the documents, determine which of the three candidate radiators are expected to keep acceptable performance over the experiment lifetime. Exclude any candidate that clearly fails the lifetime/performance requirement; if none clearly fail, keep all three for simulation."},{"id":"s3","description":"For each remaining candidate radiator, run simulate_separation at thicknesses 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 cm. Record all returned pion/kaon separation values in sigma using record_results."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best simulated thickness for each candidate, including whether performance saturates or decreases with increasing thickness. If the maximum is at an endpoint or the trend is ambiguous, run additional simulate_separation points at intermediate thicknesses near the best value, such as 0.5 cm spacing within the allowed 1–6 cm range, and record the results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare the best lifetime-qualified candidate/thickness combinations by their recorded pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c. Select the single radiator and thickness with the highest separation that satisfies all constraints, and summarize the numeric evidence for the reporting module."}]}

output.arguments: {"option":"Radiator-R1","thickness_cm":4,"justification":"Recommend Radiator-R1 at 4 cm.
